extracted.intended_audience: advanced undergraduate or beginning graduate students in mathematics studying multivariable calculus/real analysis
extracted.subtask_description: Statements, definitions, and criteria from a textbook chapter on calculus in several real variables covering operator norms, differentiability, partial derivatives, the chain rule, Taylor's theorem, vector-valued integration, and the matrix exponential. Useful as standards for correct definitions, hypotheses, and conclusions in proofs and problem solving in multivariable analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operator norm definition
rubrics_metrics.description: For T in L(F^n, F^m), there exists finite M with |T(x)| ≤ M |x| for all x in F^n; the operator norm ||T|| is the infimum of such M and equals sup_{|x|≤1} |T(x)| = sup_{|x|=1} |T(x)|.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This yields uniform continuity of linear maps on the whole space. The definition is scale-invariant: ||cT|| = |c| ||T|| and ||T|| = 0 iff T = 0. Use supremum on unit sphere to compute ||T|| in practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic properties of the operator norm
rubrics_metrics.description: Operator norm satisfies linearity and subadditivity relations: ||cT|| = |c| ||T||; ||S+T|| ≤ ||S||+||T||; ||T S|| ≤ ||T|| ||S|| for composition; ||I|| = 1 when appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These properties justify using the operator norm to define a metric on L(F^n,F^m) by d(T,S)=||T-S|| and to control compositions and linear combinations in estimates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hilbert–Schmidt norm (entrywise / Frobenius) definition
rubrics_metrics.description: The Hilbert–Schmidt norm of T is (Σ_{j=1}^n |T(e_j)|^2)^{1/2} (equivalently the Euclidean norm of the associated m×n matrix regarded in F^{mn}). It satisfies analogous norm properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful as an alternative norm on L(F^n,F^m); simpler to compute entry-by-entry and to translate between pointwise matrix convergence and operator behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalence of operator and Hilbert–Schmidt norms
rubrics_metrics.description: The norms are related by ||T|| ≤ ||T||_{HS} ≤ sqrt(n) ||T||; consequently the metrics they induce are equivalent (identity map is uniformly continuous with uniformly continuous inverse).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convergence in operator norm is equivalent to entrywise convergence of associated matrices; one may freely switch between these norms when discussing open sets, convergent sequences, and Cauchy sequences in L(F^n,F^m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Metric on space of linear maps
rubrics_metrics.description: Define d(T,S)=||T-S|| (operator norm) to make L(F^n,F^m) into a metric space; the usual metric properties hold because of operator norm properties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This metric is used when discussing limits of linear maps (e.g., derivative maps) and continuity of maps into L(F^n,F^m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of differentiability (multivariable)
rubrics_metrics.description: f: E ⊂ R^n → R^m is differentiable at x if there exists a linear T in L(R^n,R^m) such that lim_{h→0} (f(x+h)-f(x)-T(h))/|h| = 0. The linear T (if it exists) is unique and denoted f'(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniqueness follows by considering the difference of two candidates and scaling arguments. Differentiability implies continuity of f at x; if f' exists at every point it defines a function f':E→L(R^n,R^m).

rubrics_metrics.name: Jacobian and partial derivatives when derivative exists
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is differentiable at x, then all partial derivatives ∂f_i/∂x_j(x) exist, and the derivative f'(x) is the linear map whose matrix (Jacobian) has entries ∂f_i/∂x_j(x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In other words, differentiability forces the Jacobian matrix to be the matrix of partials. Compute directional/partial derivatives by testing along coordinate directions e_j and taking dot products with basis vectors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of derivative implies continuity of partials and conversely under hypotheses
rubrics_metrics.description: If f'(x) exists for all x in an open set E and x↦f'(x) is continuous at x0, then each partial ∂f_i/∂x_j is continuous at x0. Conversely, if all partials exist in E and each ∂f_i/∂x_j is continuous at x0, then f is differentiable at x0 (hence f' exists at x0). If partials are continuous on E then f is C^1 on E.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses mean value theorem along coordinate directions and bounds showing the remainder tends to zero. This gives a practical sufficient test for differentiability: check existence and continuity of first partials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of C^k and smoothness
rubrics_metrics.description: f is C^1 on E if f' exists on E and x↦f'(x) is continuous. Iterating, f is C^k if all partial derivatives up to order k exist and are continuous on E; C^∞ (smooth) means C^k for all k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalently, all l-th order partial derivatives exist and are continuous for l ≤ k. Note: the text warns some authors use 'smooth' differently for curves, but here smooth = C^∞.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interchange of mixed partial derivatives (Clairaut / Schwarz condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f: E ⊂ R^2 → R has ∂^2 f/∂y∂x defined in a neighborhood and ∂^2 f/∂y∂x is continuous at (a,b), then the mixed partial ∂^2 f/∂x∂y(a,b) exists and equals ∂^2 f/∂y∂x(a,b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses a two-variable mean value argument and estimates showing the symmetric difference tends to zero. More generally, for scalar-valued C^k functions, mixed partials of order ≤ k may be interchanged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chain rule (multivariable)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f:E⊂R^n→R^m is differentiable at x and g is differentiable at f(x) (with appropriate domains), then g∘f is differentiable at x and (g∘f)'(x) = g'(f(x)) · f'(x) (composition of linear maps / Jacobian matrices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proof constructs remainders for f and g and shows the composed remainder tends to zero. Use matrix/Jacobian multiplication to compute component formulas (classic chain rule).

rubrics_metrics.name: Taylor's theorem (multivariable) with integral remainder
rubrics_metrics.description: If F is C^N on an open set E and the segment from x to x+h lies in E, then F(x+h) = F(x) + sum_{1≤|α|≤N} (1/α!) D^α F(x) h^α + remainder, where α are multi-indices and the remainder has an integral form involving D^{N+1}F along the segment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The one-variable Taylor theorem applied to the function t↦F(x+th) together with the chain rule yields the multivariable expansion. Coefficients involve multinomial factors; the remainder is given by an integral over s in [0,1].

rubrics_metrics.name: Vector-valued partial derivatives and extension of scalar results
rubrics_metrics.description: All definitions and results about partial derivatives, chain rule, and Taylor's theorem extend to functions f:E→R^m (or C^m) by applying componentwise or by identifying C^m with R^{2m}. The Jacobian consists of vector-valued partial derivative columns.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Componentwise application is recommended rather than reworking proofs; one must ensure integrals and derivatives are interpreted vectorwise (componentwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Inequality for Riemann integrals of vector-valued functions
rubrics_metrics.description: For F:[a,b]→R^m (or C^m) Riemann integrable, |∫_a^b F(t) dt| ≤ ∫_a^b |F(t)| dt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proof uses inner product with an arbitrary unit vector u and the scalar inequality plus Schwarz to bound the norm of the integral by integral of the norm. Trivial if the integral is the zero vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: Matrix exponential via power series
rubrics_metrics.description: For any n×n complex matrix A, define exp(A)=Σ_{N=0}^∞ A^N/N!. The series converges entrywise; each entry's series is uniformly convergent on bounded sets of matrix space, and partial derivatives (for functions of matrices) are uniformly convergent on bounded sets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use operator norm bounds: ||A^N|| ≤ ||A||^N and comparison with scalar exponential series to get uniform convergence on {A:||A||≤M}. The Hilbert–Schmidt/entrywise viewpoint shows termwise differentiation is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Differentiability implies continuity (reminder)
rubrics_metrics.description: If f is differentiable at x then f is continuous at x because the linear approximation T(h) is continuous and the remainder term tends to zero as h→0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is used repeatedly to justify plugging in limit arguments and to deduce continuity of f from existence of f'.
